Daily Exchange Rates, Currency Converter and Gold Prices Worldwide

FX Rate Live helps travellers, freelancers, expats, students, online shoppers and businesses around the world check indicative exchange rates and precious metal prices before they convert money. We show mid-market (interbank) rates, the reference rates banks use when trading with each other. Banks, card providers and airport kiosks usually add a margin of 1% to 5% on top of this rate, so knowing the mid-market rate helps you spot a fair deal.

What you can do on FX Rate Live

  • Currency Converter: Convert between 30 major currencies including USD, EUR, GBP, JPY, CAD, AUD, AED, SAR, SGD and INR.
  • Gold and Silver Prices: Track spot gold (XAU/USD) and silver, plus local prices such as 24K and 22K gold in India.
  • Forex Calculators: Pip value, margin, position size and profit calculators for traders.
  • Salary Converter: Compare a job offer or salary across countries in your home currency.
  • Remittance and Tax Tools: Estimate costs of sending money abroad, including country-specific rules such as India's TCS on foreign remittance.

Why your bank or card rate is different

The rate shown here is the mid-market rate. When you buy a foreign currency, the provider sells it to you at a slightly higher rate, and when you sell, it buys at a lower rate. That difference is the spread. For example, if EUR/USD is 1.0800 at mid-market and your card charges 1.1000, you pay about 1.85% extra. On a $3,000 trip budget, that is roughly $55 lost to the exchange rate alone, before any foreign transaction fees.

What moves exchange rates

Currencies react mainly to interest rate decisions by central banks such as the US Federal Reserve, the European Central Bank, the Bank of England, the Bank of Japan and the Reserve Bank of India. Inflation reports, employment data, GDP growth, oil prices, trade balances and global risk sentiment also play a big part. When markets are nervous, investors often move into the US dollar, Swiss franc, Japanese yen and gold.

Tips before you convert or send money

  • Use the mid-market rate as your benchmark and compare two or three providers.
  • Look at the total cost: exchange margin plus transfer or card fees.
  • When paying abroad by card, choose to pay in the local currency, not your home currency, to avoid dynamic currency conversion markups.
  • Avoid converting on weekends and holidays, when spreads are often wider.
  • Check local tax rules on international transfers in your country.

Our data and its limits

Rates on FX Rate Live are indicative and for information only. We reference public benchmarks such as central bank reference rates, the LBMA for precious metals and major market data, but these are not dealing rates. Always confirm the final rate with your bank or provider before you transact. FX Rate Live does not transfer money or give investment advice.
